answers.stem_only: The application code uses the task role (task IAM role) for its AWS API calls. Grant only s3:GetObject (and ListBucket if needed) on that bucket to the task role; the task execution role is for the ECS agent (image pull, logs, secrets) and stays empty.
DaemonSets do not run on EKS Fargate because there are no nodes to manage. Run the log agent as a sidecar container in each pod spec (keep application and agent as separate containers).

Use Amazon EFS as a shared, multi-AZ, durable file system mounted as a volume in the Fargate task definition; ephemeral storage, bind mounts and per-task EBS volumes are not shared and do not survive task replacement.

Lambda tops out at 15 minutes and cannot be raised, so a 2-3 hour job needs containers. Run it as a standalone ECS task on Fargate started by the application with RunTask for each request; no servers, no idle cost.
Capacity provider strategy with FARGATE base 2 (the always-on minimum, not interruptible) and FARGATE_SPOT carrying the higher weight for the variable, interruption-tolerant extra tasks.
Interruption-tolerant, intermittent batch work on Fargate: run on Fargate Spot (FARGATE_SPOT capacity provider); no commitment because usage is not steady.

Image pulls from private ECR are made by the ECS agent / Fargate on behalf of the task using the task execution role. Grant the ECR pull permissions (GetAuthorizationToken, BatchGetImage, GetDownloadUrlForLayer, BatchCheckLayerAvailability) to the task execution role only.

ECR pull through cache rule with Docker Hub as upstream; Docker Hub needs credentials stored in a Secrets Manager secret. Tasks pull through the ECR cache URI and ECR keeps the cached images in sync with the upstream.

Fargate uses awsvpc mode, so the ALB target group must use the ip target type. For private image pulls with no internet route: interface endpoints for ecr.api and ecr.dkr plus a gateway endpoint for S3 (image layers live in S3); add only the endpoints needed (logs endpoint if awslogs is used).

Move to Amazon EKS (managed control plane) with managed node groups (or Fargate) and keep using the existing manifests and kubectl; EKS Anywhere is for on-premises, self-managed Kubernetes on EC2 adds overhead, ECS needs a rewrite.
Steady, uninterruptible Fargate usage: keep on-demand FARGATE and buy a Compute Savings Plan, which applies to Fargate (EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not; Spot can be interrupted).

Attach the Auto Scaling group as an ECS capacity provider with managed scaling (target capacity 100 percent so no spare instances are kept), and use a binpack placement strategy so tasks concentrate on few instances and empty instances can be scaled in.
